searchText: Do we expect that as soon as there is a "highly credible date" for withdrawals being enabled (e.g. it's specifically included in a HF) or post-withdrawals-enabled, that there'll be an inflow of Ether to the beaconchain? (there may/will still be a net outflow initially) I suspect not, people who haven't deposited yet will likely wait for withdrawals to be enabled. Without a set date, there are likely some agents who would not be willing to lock up their Ether (and maintain a node) who otherwise would be. So you reckon it's more about the ability to withdraw on demand, than the confidence that one could do so by a particular date? Such agents certainly exist. 🙂 The motivating question is "how will the security vs time curve look like, once withdrawals are enabled". However, I wouldn't recommend anyone rely on a set date (even if one was announced) for making financial decisions. Bear in mind that this should also bring skimming, so lots of genesis validators sitting on 3+ ETH rewards may want to reinvest. As to if the inputs outweigh the outputs, I doubt anyone really knows due to the number of participants out there. Are there any withdrawal methods that are lower burden on the beaconchain for skimming than they are for complete exits? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2759#issuecomment-988803796 skimming is healthier for the beacon chain than an exit/re-entry because validator churn in general isn't good for either the validator or the chain.
